turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have on the essay.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Who pulled this history, and was it before the zero went in or after?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.

Hale, you still haven't said whether Owen saw this before the zero went in. Whatever that history shows, none of it goes on his record, and none of it is discussed in front of his class. I want that in writing.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Students misquote plays all the time. A wrong line in Owen's essay is a wrong line. What else do you have?
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
Turn the screen. I'm searching it myself, tonight, and I'll want those two pages in an email. So what exactly are you proposing?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a week of drafting at home. Everyone writes differently under a clock. I'm reading both pages, so give me a minute.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.
Fine. We'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him. I want it in my inbox tonight: private, nothing on his file, and the zero out of the gradebook until it's marked.
Will he do it?
He will, once your email says what you just said. When is the rewrite?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in the meeting that Owen will sit a private supervised rewrite under your procedure, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still need the zero out of the gradebook until the rewrite is marked, and a date for the rewrite. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him, and she still wants written confirmation, the zero out of the gradebook until marking, and a date for the rewrite; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You owned the zero going in before the call home, then showed her three dated things she could check herself, the version history, the line that is not in the play, and his in-class writing beside the essay, and you answered each of her defences with something checkable.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether Owen saw the history before the zero unanswered, which kept her sharp and guarded for a few turns.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits just before midnight the night before the essay was due, came very close to that night, which is why she wrote the times down and pushed on procedure instead; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who pulled the history and whether Owen saw it before the zero, answer that early and plainly, and have a date ready for the rewrite when she asks for it.
